nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why is more research warranted according to Ulibarri et al. (2023)?
nodes.answer: More research is warranted to investigate how contextual differences shape the drivers behind CGR formation, aiming to better manage the turbulent period surrounding the establishment of new collaborations.

nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: Which universities are associated with the research discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Edith Cowan University and Stanford University are mentioned as being associated with the research.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Research & development|Research partnerships_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How is the co-production of knowledge expected to impact research?
nodes.answer: The co-production of knowledge, involving collaboration between researchers and stakeholders, is assumed to enhance the societal impact of research.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Research & development|Research partnerships_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the current state of empirical research on the institutionalisation of co-production of knowledge?
nodes.answer: The empirical research is fragmented and inconclusive, with a focus on specific approaches and projects rather than the views of stakeholders.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Research & development|Research partnerships_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What outcome did the data collected during and after the application of the framework indicate?
nodes.answer: The data indicated that the approach effectively stimulated a greater understanding and application of a critical co-production lens in the engagement planning of the research teams.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Research & development|Research partnerships_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What empirical question do the authors pose regarding supporting researcher teams?
nodes.answer: The authors pose the question of how researcher teams can be best supported to apply a critical co-production lens relatively rapidly within their engagement work.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Research & development|Research partnerships_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What do newly formed research teams benefit from in terms of co-production?
nodes.answer: Newly formed research teams benefit from more structured exploration and reflection on foundational elements of co-production within their intended research settings.
